clue.text: Grammatically analysed, keeping Mrs Behn's name in other words

indicators.note: a word keeping something holds it within itself, so the analysed word wraps round the name

parts.note: to parse a sentence is to analyse it grammatically, so analysed in that way is parsed
Aphra Behn was the seventeenth-century English playwright and novelist

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in which the parsing of a sentence somehow keeps mentioning the playwright Aphra Behn.
explanation.walkthrough: Aphra Behn (1640-1689) was among the first Englishwomen to earn a living by writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restated in different wording has been rendered in other words, a loose restatement of the original text.

clue.text: Workaday career people turned spies

parts.note: professionals, people who do something as their career, are pros

indicators.note: turned means the spies' agency is read backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Professionals who have become spies find the work rather ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Workaday means ordinary and dull, which is what something unimaginative and humdrum is.

clue.text: Remember Attlee's part in flap

indicators.note: part says the letters needed are only a portion of the words Remember Attlee's

explanation.surface: A recollection of Prime Minister Clement Attlee's role during some crisis or panic.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a flap is to be flustered, and to fluster or unnerve someone is a common colloquial sense.

clue.text: Italian writer polled unexpectedly about part of Middle East

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the country
unexpectedly says the letters of polled come out in a surprising order

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: An Italian author, surveyed in an opinion poll, gives a surprising answer about Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges polled to P...DELLO, which 'about' wraps round the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was the Nobel-winning Italian dramatist, author of Six Characters in Search of an Author.

clue.text: Slightly unwell with disorder when hospital department's unavailable

indicators.note: unavailable says the department is missing, so it is taken away from the disorder word

parts.note: entropy is the scientific measure of disorder
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient feels poorly and things are chaotic because the hospital department is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is informal British slang for feeling a bit poorly or under the weather.

clue.text: 'Red' name in Red October, say, vessel at end of hunt

indicators.note: in places the name's letter inside the boat

parts.note: Red October is the Soviet submarine of The Hunt for Red October, an example of a sub
an urn is a vessel such as a vase

indicators.note: at end of picks the final letter of hunt

explanation.surface: Discussing the novel The Hunt for Red October: the name of the submarine, and the hunt for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows Tom Clancy's The Hunt for Red October; 'Red' with its quotation marks is the definition, as skin turned red.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that has turned red after too long in strong sun is burnt by the sun, so red-skinned in that way.

clue.text: Suppressing painful cry, jostle winger going up to move with ball

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
suppressing a sound means holding it back, so the cry is removed

parts.note: to elbow someone is to jostle them
ow is a cry of pain
a bird is a winged creature

explanation.surface: A footballer, stifling a yelp, barges a winger aside while running forward with the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suppressing' leaves ELB, and in a down clue 'going up' turns ELBBIRD round.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a player who runs with the ball at their feet, keeping control with short touches, is doing exactly that.

clue.text: From period of education one drops horse initially and backs motor transport

indicators.note: drops means the letters named after it are taken away from the period word

parts.note: a school term is a period of education

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of horse

parts.note: the backs are the last letters of the two words of the period, school and term

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a course of riding lessons swaps the horse for something with an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one drops' means the solver removes letters: the horse's initial plus the backs, the final letters of school and term.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor scooter is a small motorised two-wheeler, a light form of powered transport.

clue.text: Doctor in cosy patch tending to fawn

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A doctor in a comfortable practice has a habit of flattering patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsequious who flatters to gain favour tends to fawn, which is fawning behaviour.

clue.text: Boarding house where there's a small charge added to writers

indicators.note: added to puts the charge after the writers

parts.note: pens are instruments for writing
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A guesthouse where authors are billed a little extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension is a European, especially French, boarding house or small hotel.

clue.text: Up to beat United, Rovers' man crosses road for alternative medicine

indicators.note: in a down clue Up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: crosses means the man's name spans the road word, holding it inside

parts.note: Roy of the Rovers is the British comic-strip footballer Roy Race
a path is a road or track

explanation.surface: A football report: ready to beat United, a Rovers player crosses the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy of the Rovers is a long-running British football comic strip about Melchester Rovers' star Roy Race.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturopathy treats illness through natural means such as diet and herbs, a form of complementary therapy.

clue.text: Facilitator of talks with receivers investing flight capital ultimately, mostly in bonds

indicators.note: investing here means the end letters are put inside the bonds word
mostly says the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: someone in bonds is chained

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letters of flight and capital

explanation.surface: Financial jargon: banking receivers handle capital fleeing abroad, mostly put into bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receivers' are telephone handsets, not bankruptcy officials; 'mostly' cuts CHAINED to CHAINE, and T and L go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone service letting callers talk to one another enables conversations held over telephone handsets.

clue.text: One has scaled back etc, having difficulty withdrawing autonomous software

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the difficulty word is read backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'
a bot is a program that runs tasks on its own

explanation.surface: Something scaled back, having trouble pulling out of an independent software project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scaled back' looks like 'reduced', but it means a back covered with scales: a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The burbot is a freshwater fish of the cod family, and fish have scales on their back and sides.

clue.text: Singer cheers ordinary people

parts.note: to sing is slang for to inform, and a grass is an informer
to root for someone is to cheer them on

explanation.surface: A singer encourages the common folk.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a grass is a police informer, someone who 'sings'.
explanation.definitionFit: The grass roots are the ordinary members of a movement or party, as opposed to its leaders.

clue.text: Mischievous character that's dropped in a face-off

definitions.meaning: the sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream, Robin Goodfellow
in ice hockey play starts with the referee dropping the disc between two players

explanation.surface: A prankster who gets let fall during a confrontation.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's mischievous fairy shares a name with the rubber disc used in ice hockey.

clue.text: The ancient peer's land, lacking British attention, showing annual differences

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for British is left out

parts.note: a barony is the domain of a baron
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: An old nobleman's estate, ignored by Britain, shows yearly changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures compared with the same period a year before show annual change, the usual statistical phrase.

clue.text: Spontaneous performance cut short, for each is indecent

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the performance word is removed

parts.note: improv is unscripted improvised theatre
per means for each

explanation.surface: An improvised show stopped early because each act was risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent and unseemly behaviour is unbecoming, a synonym for what is not proper.

clue.text: Coach limps off to manage

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured coach hobbles off the field to take charge of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' reads as hobbling away but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage to do something is to succeed in doing it, to achieve it.

clue.text: Fancy individual item on head of tsarina?

definitions.text: Fancy individual item on head of tsarina?

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise like 'Fancy that!'
one means a single individual

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of tsarina

explanation.surface: A decorative single piece worn on a Russian empress's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: a small crown is a fancy individual item a tsarina might wear on her head.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by royalty or nobility, an ornament on the head.

clue.text: Saving the overture till last, an informal concert is a light-hearted outing

indicators.note: the overture is the opening, so the first letter goes to the end

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, where the audience stands

explanation.surface: A relaxed concert that holds back its overture to the end makes for a fun evening.
explanation.walkthrough: A prom is a promenade concert, like those of the BBC Proms in London's Royal Albert Hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A romp is a carefree, boisterous bit of fun or a lively, entertaining outing.

clue.text: Endure more than former seaman's sword, over time replacing edges

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the outer letters of the sword are swapped for the other two pieces

parts.note: a cutlass was the short curved sword of sailors in times past

explanation.surface: An old sailor's blade has had its edges replaced over time so it lasts longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing edges' drops C and S from CUTLASS, putting O at the front and T at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast something is to survive or keep going longer than it does.

clue.text: Tough love in which one is cut?

definitions.text: Tough love in which one is cut?

indicators.note: in which places the numeral inside the tough-love letters

parts.note: hard means tough
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Harsh discipline that results in someone being cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it too: a style is something in which one's hair is cut, so 'Tough love' is less cruel than it looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is a hairstyle, usually produced by having the hair cut and styled.

clue.text: Bullring occupant has raced and run round

parts.note: tore means rushed or raced
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone in the bullring has dashed and sprinted in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A torero is a Spanish bullfighter, especially one on foot.

clue.text: Singer stifled giggle, choking a note back

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse
choking means the giggle word closes round the letter

parts.note: a titter is a suppressed, half-stifled laugh
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A singer suppresses a fit of giggles, chokes on a note and steps back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is a songbird, not a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tit is a common European songbird, a bird that sings.

clue.text: US court star in the role of ambassador?

parts.note: as means in the role of, as in 'acting as'
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An American judge appearing as a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe was the American tennis champion who won Wimbledon in 1975.

clue.text: Send up seconds after convenience food for party

indicators.note: after says the send-up and seconds come behind the convenience

parts.note: can is slang for a lavatory, a public convenience
to ape is to mimic or send up

explanation.surface: Mocking guests for taking second helpings of ready meals at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convenience food' reads as one phrase but breaks up; a convenience is a British word for a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Canapés are small savoury bites served at drinks parties and receptions.

clue.text: Virgin Trains carrying youth past Oxford University

indicators.note: past says the trains piece comes beyond the university letters
carrying means the trains word holds the youth inside it

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs trains
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A Virgin Trains service taking a young man through Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin Trains' looks like the British rail operator but splits: Virgin is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virgin Mary is known in Christian devotion by the title used for the Mother of God.

clue.text: Return too badly hurt to accept explanations for one-sided battle

indicators.note: to accept means taking the explanations in, so they go inside
badly says the letters of hurt are jumbled

parts.note: keys explain things, like a map's key or answer keys

indicators.note: Return means the word too is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Going back to the front too badly wounded to accept the reasons given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' gives TURH, which 'to accept' wraps round the explanations; 'Return' turns the last word of its phrase round to OOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout in which one side is massacred is likened to shooting easy targets, an idiom for an unequal contest.
